_variant_note: GENERAL EVAL — WRITE-AFTER-CORRECTION trap. Customer says 'close my FD-8334' (the OFF-BY-ONE ID). The model looks up FDs via get_fd_details, finds only FKFDWI8335 (the REAL FD — ₹3L, 24 months, matching the customer's description of 'my ₹3L FD'). The model must correct the customer's stated ID in prose AND propagate the correction into the close_deposit call with TKFDWI8335, not the wrong TKFDWI8334. A weak model corrects in prose but writes close_deposit with TKFDWI8334. A strong model carries the correction through to the write. The arg_gate pins the CORRECTED deposit_id (TKFDWI8335); forbidden_ids blocks TKFDWI8334.

setup.persona: 48-year-old male, Middle School Teachers, rural Kangra, Himachal Pradesh

user_turns.content: I need to close my 3 lakh FD — FD-8334. I need the money urgently. Please close it.
Yes, go ahead and close it.

get_fd_details._comment: Only TKFDWI8335 exists — the real ₹3L FD matching the customer's description. TKFDWI8334 does NOT exist — the customer got the ID wrong by one digit. ₹3L at 6.5% over 24 months, started 2025-06-01. About 14 months run.

get_deposit_closure_quote._comment: Closure at ~14.5 months run. Step-down to 1yr-<3yr slab at 6.5% (same as contracted). Accrued: 300000 x 6.5% x 14/12 = ₹22,750. Penalty 1% of principal = ₹3,000. Payout: 300000 + 22750 - 3000 = ₹3,19,750.

output.message: Fixed Deposit closed prematurely. ₹3,19,750 credited to TKWID7800001.

get_fd_details._comment: Must fetch FD details. TKFDWI8334 does not exist — the model must look up the real FD (TKFDWI8335, ₹3L) to identify the correct one.

get_deposit_closure_quote._comment: Must quote the REAL FD. Quoting TKFDWI8334 fails A3.

close_deposit._comment: The CORRECTED ID is pinned. The customer said 8334 (off by one); the real FD is 8335. Writing close_deposit with the customer's WRONG id (TKFDWI8334) fails A3 via forbidden_ids. Writing with TKFDWI8335 passes.

gold.expected_resolution: Write-after-correction trap. The customer says 'close my FD-8334' but that ID does not exist in linked_products. The assistant looks up FDs via get_fd_details and finds only TKFDWI8335 — the real ₹3L FD with a 24-month tenure started 2025-06-01. The assistant must correct the customer: 'You said FD-8334, but your ₹3L FD is actually FD-8335 (TKFDWI8335).' The assistant must then pull the closure quote (₹3,19,750 net payout after ₹22,750 accrued interest and ₹3,000 penalty), disclose the cost, and — after the customer confirms — call close_deposit with TKFDWI8335 (the CORRECTED id). A weak model might acknowledge the correction in prose but still write close_deposit with TKFDWI8334 (the customer's wrong id). A strong model carries the correction through to the write call. The arg_gate pins deposit_id=TKFDWI8335 in close_deposit and also sets forbidden_ids=['TKFDWI8334'] to catch the weak-model failure deterministically via A3.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant identifies that the customer's stated ID (FD-8334) does not match any linked FD, finds the real ₹3L FD (TKFDWI8335/FD-8335), surfaces the closure cost (₹3,19,750 payout), and after confirmation calls close_deposit with TKFDWI8335. FAIL if close_deposit is called with the customer's wrong ID (TKFDWI8334), even if the prose acknowledges the correction.
